description: Core linguistic vocabulary — units of language (phoneme to discourse), grammatical categories, syntactic roles, sentence types. The agent's foundation for talking about language at all. Built per the structuralist tradition (Saussure, Bloomfield, Chomsky) without committing to any single theoretical school.

concepts.name: phoneme
concepts.definition: Minimal contrastive unit of sound in a language. Identified by minimal pair tests. The phoneme /p/ in English contrasts with /b/ (pat vs bat).

concepts.name: morpheme
concepts.definition: Minimal meaningful unit of grammar. May be free (stand alone: 'cat') or bound (attached: '-s' plural marker). Distinct from word — 'cats' contains two morphemes.

concepts.name: lexeme
concepts.definition: Abstract unit underlying a set of word-forms. 'run', 'runs', 'ran', 'running' are forms of the lexeme RUN. The dictionary headword.

concepts.name: word
concepts.definition: Free morpheme or compound thereof that can stand alone in an utterance. Bounded by spaces in writing systems with word-spacing.

concepts.name: phrase
concepts.definition: Group of words functioning as a single unit, headed by a particular category (noun phrase, verb phrase, prepositional phrase). Building block of clauses.

concepts.name: clause
concepts.definition: Syntactic unit with a subject and a predicate. May be independent (main clause) or dependent (subordinate clause).

concepts.name: sentence
concepts.definition: Maximal syntactic unit, typically containing at least one main clause. In writing, bounded by sentence-final punctuation.

concepts.name: paragraph
concepts.definition: Discourse unit grouping sentences around a coherent topic. In writing, marked by indentation or vertical space.

concepts.name: discourse
concepts.definition: Connected stretch of language above the sentence level. The site of coherence, cohesion, topic management, and pragmatic inference.

concepts.name: syntax
concepts.definition: Branch of linguistics concerned with how words combine into phrases, clauses, sentences. The structural side of grammar.

concepts.name: semantics
concepts.definition: Branch of linguistics concerned with literal meaning — denotation, sense, reference, truth-conditional content.

concepts.name: pragmatics
concepts.definition: Branch of linguistics concerned with meaning in context — implicature, speech acts, presupposition, deixis, conversational inference.

concepts.name: noun
concepts.definition: Part-of-speech category for words referring to entities, concepts, kinds, instances. Subject and object roles typically filled by nouns.

concepts.name: verb
concepts.definition: Part-of-speech category for words denoting actions, states, processes. Heads predicates; carries tense, aspect, mood, voice.

concepts.name: adjective
concepts.definition: Part-of-speech category for words modifying nouns by attributing properties. Pre- or post-nominal depending on language.

concepts.name: adverb
concepts.definition: Part-of-speech category for words modifying verbs, adjectives, other adverbs, or whole clauses. Encode manner, degree, time, place.

concepts.name: preposition
concepts.definition: Part-of-speech for words heading prepositional phrases — encode spatial, temporal, logical relations between entities.

concepts.name: pronoun
concepts.definition: Part-of-speech for words substituting for noun phrases — anaphoric (refer back), deictic (refer to context), or interrogative.

concepts.name: determiner
concepts.definition: Part-of-speech for words specifying reference of a noun phrase — articles (a, the), demonstratives (this, that), quantifiers (some, all).

concepts.name: subject
concepts.definition: Syntactic role: the noun phrase whose referent is the topic of the predicate. Typically nominative-case-marked, agrees with the verb.

concepts.name: object
concepts.definition: Syntactic role: the noun phrase argument of a transitive verb. Direct object (acted upon); indirect object (recipient/beneficiary).

concepts.name: predicate
concepts.definition: Syntactic role: the part of a clause that says something about the subject. Headed by a verb (or sometimes a copula + complement).

concepts.name: modifier
concepts.definition: Syntactic role: a phrase adding optional information to its head (adjective modifying noun; adverb modifying verb).

concepts.name: tense
concepts.definition: Grammatical category locating an event in time relative to the moment of speaking — past, present, future.

concepts.name: aspect
concepts.definition: Grammatical category encoding the temporal flow or completeness of an event — perfective (bounded), imperfective (ongoing), perfect (resultative).

concepts.name: voice
concepts.definition: Grammatical category encoding the relation between the subject and the action — active (subject is agent), passive (subject is patient).

concepts.name: declarative
concepts.definition: Sentence type that makes a statement. Has falsifiable truth conditions; the prototypical input to factual reasoning.

concepts.name: interrogative
concepts.definition: Sentence type that asks a question. Yes/no (polar) or wh- (content). Expects an answer; not directly truth-evaluable.

concepts.name: imperative
concepts.definition: Sentence type that issues a command, request, or instruction. Subjectless (implied 'you'); demands action.

rules.name: a_declarative_sentence_asserts_a_proposition
then: the proposition is a candidate atomic fact for the substrate's reasoning
rules.why: Declaratives are the workhorse of factual prose. Identifying them is the first step in extracting claims from text.

rules.name: a_clause_has_a_subject_and_a_predicate
if: a Sentence (or subordinate Clause) is syntactically well-formed
then: it contains a predicate phrase headed by a verb
rules.why: Identifying subject + predicate is the minimum structural decomposition needed to ask 'what is being claimed about what'.

rules.name: a_pronoun_requires_anaphoric_or_deictic_resolution
then: the pronoun has an antecedent in nearby discourse OR a deictic referent in context
answering questions about the referent requires resolving it first
rules.why: Unresolved pronouns block claim-extraction — the substrate cannot match a question's keywords against a Sentence whose subject is 'it'.

rules.name: a_phrase_is_classified_by_its_head_category
then: it has a head — a single word that determines its syntactic category
the phrase is classified as noun-phrase / verb-phrase / etc. by its head
rules.why: Head-based classification is the substrate's hook for matching question keywords against phrase referents.

rules.name: tense_locates_an_event_in_time
if: a Sentence contains a tensed verb
then: the Sentence's claim has a temporal anchor (past, present, future)
matching the Sentence against time-bounded questions requires honoring its tense
rules.why: Research text is full of tense-laden claims ('Najman classified', 'will be shown'); tense matters for the substrate's relevance scoring.

rules.name: an_interrogative_sentence_seeks_information_not_asserts_it
then: the Sentence does NOT contribute a candidate fact
the Sentence indicates a query the agent should attend to
rules.why: Distinguishing questions from assertions prevents the substrate from extracting question text as if it were claims.
